mainTopic: The סוטה ceremony and the court's pressure on her, stories of יהודה and ראובן confessing, and whether the משנה proves that a receipt (שובר) is written
overview: The משנה finishes describing how the כהן strips the סוטה of her jewelry and dignity, and who may and may not watch. The גמרא learns from the shared word 'תורה' that her case goes before the court of seventy-one. It then sets the משנה's 'they pressure her' against a ברייתא saying the court also urges an innocent woman to drink. The answer is that the משנה speaks of the time before the scroll is erased, and the ברייתא of the time after. A ברייתא then lists the stories told to the סוטה: יהודה and ראובן admitted their sins and were rewarded. This leads to רבי יוחנן's story of יהודה's bones and משה's prayers, and to the question of why ראובן admitted in public. The גמרא next tries to prove from the משנה that a receipt (שובר) is written; אביי and רבא each block the proof. The amud ends as the גמרא begins questioning the משנה's words 'they bring her up' to the Eastern Gate, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Removing her jewelry and tying the rope
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of jewelry taken off the סוטה to make her unattractive, then says the כהן ties an Egyptian rope above her chest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her chokers, nose rings and finger rings are taken off her to make her look unattractive. Then the כהן brings an Egyptian rope and ties it above her chest.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing what the כהן does to the סוטה before she drinks. Her jewelry is removed and a plain rope is tied on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose is stated openly: כדי לנוולה, to make her unattractive. Everything that made her look beautiful is taken away. The rope is tied above her chest, which comes before she drinks the bitter water.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife suspected of unfaithfulness who is brought to drink the bitter water
Chokers, necklaces worn tight around the neck
To make her unattractive, to strip her of her beauty
An Egyptian rope, a plain rope

phrases.english: or chokers, nose rings, and finger rings —
they remove them from her, in order to make her unattractive.
And afterward he brings an Egyptian rope
and ties it above her breasts.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's jewelry is removed to make her unattractive, and an Egyptian rope is tied above her chest.

steps.title: Who may watch her
steps.stepSummary: Anyone may come and watch except her own slaves and maidservants, and all women are allowed to watch so they will learn a lesson, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who wants to watch may come, except her slaves and maidservants, because she feels bold and proud in front of them. All women may watch her, as the פסוק says: 'All the women will be warned, and will not act like your lewdness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on who may watch the סוטה ceremony. It gives one group that is kept out and one group that is welcomed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her own servants are kept away because in front of them she feels proud and bold. All women are allowed in because the scene is meant to teach them, as the פסוק from יחזקאל says.

keyTerms.meaning: Her male slaves and her maidservants
She feels bold, proud and at ease in front of them
And they will be warned or taught a lesson
Lewdness, immoral behavior

steps.whatToRemember: The ceremony is public on purpose. Her own servants are kept out because they make her feel proud, while women are welcome so they will learn from it.

phrases.english: And anyone who wants to watch may come to watch,
except for her slaves and her maidservants,
because her heart is bold in front of them.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'her heart is coarse with them': around her own servants she feels proud and at ease.

phrases.english: And all the women are permitted to watch her,
as it is said: 'And all the women will be taught a lesson
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 23:48

phrases.english: and will not act according to your lewdness.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may watch except her servants, because they make her feel bold. All women may watch so they will learn a lesson.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where we learn the משנה's rule that the סוטה is brought before the great court.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to the start of the משנה, which said the סוטה is brought to the great בית דין in ירושלים. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? A request for a source
The great court of seventy-one judges, the סנהדרין

phrases.english: GEMARA
From where do we know these matters?
phrases.notes: He means the earlier rule in the משנה that she is brought before the great בית דין in ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and asks for the משנה's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that the סוטה is brought before the court of seventy-one.

steps.title: The source: the shared word 'תורה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר גמדא, quoting רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, learns it through a גזירה שוה. The word 'התורה' appears both for the סוטה and for the court of seventy-one, so the סוטה's case also belongs before seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: We learn it from the word 'תורה' appearing in two places. Here, about the סוטה, it says 'And the כהן shall do to her all this תורה.' There it says 'According to the תורה that they will teach you.' Just as there it means a court of seventy-one, so here it means a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a גזירה שוה, linking two פסוקים that share the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים about following the court's teaching refers to the great court of seventy-one. Since the סוטה פסוק uses the same word 'התורה', the same court must be involved. So the סוטה is brought before the סנהדרין of seventy-one.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is learned from
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two different פסוקים
It is written here... and it is written there, the standard way of setting up a גזירה שוה
Seventy-one, the number of judges in the great סנהדרין

steps.whatToRemember: The source that the סוטה goes before the court of seventy-one is a גזירה שוה built on the word 'תורה'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said
that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
It is learned from 'Torah' and 'Torah'.
phrases.notes: The same word shows up in two פסוקים, and that link teaches the law. This is called a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is written here:
'And the priest shall do to her all this law',
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:30

phrases.english: and it is written there:
'According to the law that they will teach you',
phrases.notes: דברים 17:11. That פסוק is about following the great court's ruling.

phrases.english: just as there it is with seventy-one,
so too here it is with seventy-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר גַּמָּדָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָתְיָא תּוֹרָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word 'תורה' links the סוטה to the court of seventy-one described in דברים 17:11.

steps.title: Contradiction: pressuring her to drink as well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'they pressure her' and sets it against a ברייתא saying that just as the court pressures her not to drink, it also pressures her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they pressure her,' and so on. Compare it with a ברייתא: Just as they pressure her not to drink, so too they pressure her to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new topic from the משנה and points out a contradiction with a ברייתא. Step 6 finishes quoting the ברייתא, and step 7 answers the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only describes pressuring the woman to confess so she does not drink. The ברייתא says the court also pushes her to drink. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה leaves out this second kind of encouragement.

keyTerms.meaning: They pressure or frighten, applying strong persuasion
And contrast it with, a formula for raising a contradiction from another source
Etc., showing the quotation from the משנה continues

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the court never encourages her to drink. It simply does not mention it. The contradiction comes from the ברייתא adding something the משנה left out.

phrases.english: 'And they pressure her,' etc.
And contrast it with:
Just as they pressure her so that she will not drink,
so too they pressure her so that she will drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from a different line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's description of pressuring the סוטה only to confess.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the court also encourages her to drink, which the משנה does not mention, so the two sources seem to disagree.

steps.title: What the court says to encourage her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to give the court's words. If you are sure you are pure, stand firm and drink, because the water works like a dry drug that only hurts where there is already a wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say to her: My daughter, if you are sure you are pure, stand firm on your innocence and drink. The bitter water is like a dry drug placed on live flesh. If there is a wound, it soaks in and goes down. If there is no wound, it does nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא, which shows exactly how the court encourages an innocent woman to drink. This fills out the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison explains why an innocent woman has nothing to fear. A dry drug only gets into the body through an open wound, and in the same way the water only harms a woman who has sinned. These words of encouragement are exactly what the משנה leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: My daughter, a gentle way of addressing her
On your clear truth, standing firm on your innocence
The bitter water the סוטה drinks
A dry drug or powder
Soaks in and penetrates

phrases.english: They say to her: My daughter,
if the matter is clear to you
that you are pure,
stand firm on your clear truth, and drink.
For the bitter water is like nothing

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְסַם יָבֵשׁ שֶׁמּוּנָּח עַל בָּשָׂר חַי.
phrases.english: except a dry drug placed on live flesh.
If there is a wound there,
it soaks in and goes down;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם מַכָּה — אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: if there is no wound there, it does nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמְרִים לָהּ בִּתִּי אִם בָּרוּר לָךְ הַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא that raises the contradiction, giving the court's actual words of encouragement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה, which mentions only pressure to confess.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא spells out real words of encouragement to drink, which makes the משנה's silence about them stand out even more.

steps.title: Before and after the scroll is erased
steps.stepSummary: The משנה and the ברייתא speak about two different times. Before the scroll is erased, the court pressures her not to drink. After it is erased, the court pressures her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the משנה is talking about before the scroll was erased. There, the ברייתא is talking about after the scroll was erased.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא by saying each one talks about a different stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the scroll with God's name is erased, the court wants her to admit and not drink, so God's name is not erased. Once it has been erased, refusing would make the erasing pointless, so the court now pushes her to drink if she is innocent. Both sources are correct, just at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, an answer that removes a contradiction
The scroll on which the סוטה section, with God's name, is written
Was erased (into the water)

steps.whatToRemember: Before the erasing: pressure not to drink. After the erasing: pressure to drink if she is innocent.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, it is before the scroll was erased.
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the משנה, where the court pressures her not to drink.

phrases.english: There, it is after the scroll was erased.
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the ברייתא, where the court pressures her to drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 5-6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time (before versus after the erasing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seem to give opposite instructions for the same moment
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source describes a different stage of the process, so they do not argue

steps.title: What the court tells her: stories from earlier generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'he says before her' and brings a ברייתא explaining it: the court tells her teachings and stories of earlier people, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And he says before her' and so on. The rabbis taught: He says before her words of teaching and stories that happened, written in the early books, like 'which wise men told and did not hide from their fathers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and quotes a ברייתא explaining what the court actually says to the סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is to encourage her to admit if she is guilty. The פסוק about wise men who 'told and did not hide' is the opening for examples of great people who confessed. The examples come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Teachings and stories drawn from the פסוקים
The early holy writings
Hid, held back

phrases.english: And he says before her, etc.
The rabbis taught:
He says before her words of teaching,
and events that happened, in the early writings,
for example: 'Which wise men told'
phrases.notes: איוב 15:18

phrases.english: and did not hide from their fathers.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court tells the סוטה teachings and stories of earlier people who admitted their sins

steps.title: יהודה and ראובן admitted and were rewarded
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives examples: יהודה and ראובן both admitted their sins without shame, and both earned the World to Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה admitted and was not ashamed. What was his end? He inherited the life of the World to Come. ראובן admitted and was not ashamed. What was his end? He inherited the life of the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives the actual examples of people who confessed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the 'wise men who told and did not hide' from the פסוק. The message to the סוטה is: admitting is not the end of you; great people admitted and gained eternal reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Admitted, confessed
Was ashamed
Inherited
The life of the World to Come

phrases.english: Judah admitted and was not ashamed,
what was his end?
He inherited the life of the World to Come.
Reuben admitted and was not ashamed,
what was his end?
He inherited the life of the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the examples promised in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהודה and ראובן admitted their sins without shame and earned the World to Come

steps.title: What was their reward?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reward יהודה and ראובן received.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was their reward?
steps.whatsHappening: A short question is asked about their reward. The גמרא will immediately question this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question sounds strange, because the ברייתא just said their reward was the World to Come. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Their reward

phrases.english: And what was their reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the stories of יהודה and ראובן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward יהודה and ראובן received

steps.title: But we already said their reward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: why ask about their reward? It was just stated that they inherited the World to Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was their reward?! It is just as we said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself, since the answer was already given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said they got the World to Come, so asking again seems pointless. This forces the question to mean something new, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we are saying, as already stated

phrases.english: What was their reward?!
It is as we said!
phrases.notes: He means the World to Come, which was just mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the question of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The question 'what was their reward' in step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer was already stated, so the question is repetitive

steps.title: Their reward in this world
steps.stepSummary: The question really meant their reward in this world. The answer comes from the next פסוק in איוב: the land was given to them alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: what was their reward in this world? 'To them alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the question to be about reward in this world and answers it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The World to Come is the reward in the next world; the question now asks about this world. The next פסוק in איוב says the land was given to them alone, showing they were also rewarded here.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introducing a corrected version
This world
A stranger, an outsider

steps.whatToRemember: יהודה and ראובן were rewarded in both worlds: the World to Come, and the land in this world.

phrases.english: Rather: what was their reward in this world?
'To them alone the land was given,'
phrases.notes: איוב 15:19

phrases.english: and no stranger passed among them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by reframing the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to repeat the reward of the World to Come
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about reward in this world, answered by the next פסוק in איוב

steps.title: How do we know ראובן admitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says we have a פסוק showing that יהודה admitted, but asks where we see that ראובן admitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense with יהודה; we find that he admitted, as it is written: 'And יהודה recognized and said, She is more righteous than I.' But ראובן, how do we know that he admitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source that ראובן confessed. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For יהודה there is a clear פסוק where he admits about תמר. For ראובן, no such admission is written plainly, so the ברייתא's claim needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted
We have found
From where do we know?
And he recognized

phrases.english: Granted, with Judah we have found that he admitted,
as it is written: 'And Judah recognized'
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:26

phrases.english: and said: She is more righteous than I,'
but Reuben, from where do we know that he admitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions part of the ברייתא's claim in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ראובן admitted his sin

steps.title: Source for ראובן's admission: the joined blessings
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes through רבי יוחנן, who asks why the פסוק joins ראובן's blessing to יהודה's blessing with the word 'and'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does it mean that it is written 'Let ראובן live and not die,' followed by 'And this for יהודה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering where we see that ראובן admitted. It brings רבי יוחנן, who opens by asking about two פסוקים. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's blessing of יהודה starts with 'and' (וְזֹאת), which ties it to ראובן's blessing right before it. רבי יוחנן asks what links the two. His explanation will show that ראובן's admission is connected to יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (opens an explanation of a פסוק)
Let ראובן live and not die (משה's blessing)
And this for יהודה (the start of יהודה's blessing)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the meaning of what is written
"Let Reuben live and not die,"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:6

phrases.english: "And this for Judah"?
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7. The puzzle is why יהודה's blessing starts with 'and,' as if it continues ראובן's.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 13's question about where ראובן admitted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the link between ראובן's and יהודה's blessings in דברים 33, which רבי יוחנן explains next.

steps.title: יהודה's bones and משה's plea
steps.stepSummary: יהודה's bones rolled around in the coffin in the desert until משה pleaded that יהודה was the one who caused ראובן to admit.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the years Israel was in the desert, יהודה's bones rolled around in the coffin. Then משה prayed for him and said: Master of the Universe, who caused ראובן to admit? יהודה! And this is what יהודה gets?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the link. משה argued that יהודה deserved better, because יהודה's example led ראובן to admit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers step 13: ראובן's admission is hinted at in the blessing 'let ראובן live,' and משה says it came about because of יהודה. 'And this for יהודה' is read as משה's protest: is rolling bones the reward for the one who caused ראובן to admit?

keyTerms.meaning: rolling around
coffin
prayed for mercy
caused
admitted, confessed

phrases.english: All those years
that Israel was in the desert,
the bones of Judah were
rolling around in the coffin,
until Moses arose
and asked for mercy on his behalf.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
who caused Reuben to admit?
Judah!
"And this for Judah"?!
phrases.notes: משה is protesting here: is this rolling around really what יהודה gets?

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל אוֹתָן שָׁנִים שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's explanation of the joined פסוקים raised in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהודה caused ראובן to admit, and משה used this to plead for יהודה. That is why the two blessings are joined.

steps.title: משה's prayers restore יהודה step by step
steps.stepSummary: Each phrase of יהודה's blessing is a prayer of משה that was answered, fixing one problem after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, 'Hear, Lord, the voice of יהודה,' and his limbs went back into their sockets. But they did not bring him into the heavenly ישיבה, so: 'And bring him to his people.' He did not know how to debate in learning with the רבנן, so: 'His hands shall contend for him.' His learning did not come out according to the הלכה, so: 'And You shall be a help against his adversaries.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. משה keeps praying, and each phrase of the פסוק fixes the next problem until יהודה is fully restored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of דברים 33:7 is read as four answered prayers: his bones are rejoined, he is let into the heavenly ישיבה, he can debate with the רבנן, and he reaches the right הלכה. The story shows how much יהודה's admission was worth.

keyTerms.meaning: socket (where a bone fits)
the heavenly ישיבה
to give and take, debate in learning
a תורה discussion or teaching
in line with the הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: יהודה's admission was so valuable that it led ראובן to admit too, and משה used this to bring יהודה full rest and success in the heavenly ישיבה.

phrases.english: Immediately: "Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah,"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7. Each phrase from here on is another prayer of משה that was answered.

phrases.english: his limbs entered their sockets.
But they would not bring him in
to the heavenly yeshiva,
"And bring him to his people."
But he did not know how
to debate in Torah discussion
phrases.notes: Literally 'to lift and to toil,' meaning the back-and-forth of learning.

phrases.english: with the Sages,
"His hands shall contend for him."

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה קָא סָלְקָא לֵיהּ שְׁמַעְתָּא
phrases.english: His learning did not come out right
in line with the halacha,
"And You shall be a help against his adversaries."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 15 and explains the rest of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every part of יהודה's blessing is an answered prayer of משה that restored יהודה completely.

steps.title: Why did ראובן admit in public?
steps.stepSummary: יהודה had a good reason to admit, since it saved תמר. But ראובן had no such reason, and רב ששת says publicly listing your sins is brazen.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that יהודה admitted, so that תמר would not be burned. But why did ראובן need to admit? Didn't רב ששת say: I consider someone who spells out his sins to be brazen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ראובן's public admission. It uses רב ששת's rule that confessing your sins out loud in detail is brazen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה's confession saved an innocent life, so he had to speak up. ראובן's confession saved no one, so it looks like the brazenness רב ששת criticizes. The challenge asks how ראובן's admission could be praised.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense (introduces the case that is fine, before the hard one)
תמר, who was about to be burned until יהודה admitted
brazen, shameless
spells out his sins in detail

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not against regretting your sins. He is against announcing their details in public, which can show a lack of shame.

phrases.english: It makes sense that Judah admitted,
so that Tamar would not be burned.
But Reuben,
why did he need to admit?
But didn't Rav Sheshet say:
I consider brazen
one who spells out his sins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that ראובן's admission has been shown, the גמרא asks whether a public admission was proper.
steps.kashyaTarget: The praise given to ראובן for admitting his sin publicly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ששת calls spelling out your sins brazen. Unlike יהודה, ראובן had no life-saving reason to admit, so his admission seems improper.

steps.title: ראובן admitted to protect his brothers
steps.stepSummary: ראובן admitted so that his brothers would not be suspected of the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: He admitted so that his brothers would not be suspected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ראובן also had a good reason to admit. He did it to clear his brothers of suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like יהודה, ראובן spoke up to protect others, not to show off his sin. So רב ששת's criticism does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: so that, in order that
they would be suspected
his brothers

steps.whatToRemember: Admitting a sin in public is praised when it protects others: יהודה saved תמר, and ראובן cleared his brothers. Otherwise, רב ששת calls it brazen.

phrases.english: So that his brothers would not be suspected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a protective reason that takes ראובן's admission outside רב ששת's criticism.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראובן's public confession had no purpose, so it looked brazen.
steps.terutzMaskana: ראובן admitted in order to protect his brothers from suspicion, just as יהודה admitted to save תמר.

steps.title: Proof from the admitting woman that a receipt is written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a woman who admits 'I am defiled.' It concludes from the משנה that when a debt is paid, we write a receipt (שובר) and do not just tear up the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if she says 'I am defiled,' etc., she gives a receipt for her כתובה. Learn from this that we write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and pulls a general money rule out of it: when a debt is paid, the payer gets a written receipt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה says the woman 'writes a receipt' for her כתובה, the גמרא concludes that a receipt is the normal way to show a debt was paid. The other way would be to tear up the original document. This is a proof from the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing that a debt or obligation has been paid
'Learn from this': a conclusion drawn from a source
'I am defiled': the סוטה admits she sinned
The marriage contract that promises the wife money at divorce or widowhood

phrases.english: If she says: 'I am defiled,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The 'etc.' covers the rest of the line: she gives a receipt for her כתובה.

phrases.english: Learn from this: one writes a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן and ראובן material and goes back to the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a receipt is written when a debt is paid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording that the admitting סוטה 'writes a receipt' for her כתובה

steps.title: אביי rereads the משנה as 'she tears'
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. He says the משנה should be read as 'she tears' her כתובה, not 'she writes a receipt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: read the משנה as 'she tears' the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof by changing how the משנה is read. If she tears the כתובה, there is no proof about receipts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the word 'receipt.' אביי says the correct reading is that the woman tears up her כתובה. Once the word 'receipt' is gone, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: She tears (the document)

phrases.english: Abaye said: Teach: 'she tears.'
phrases.notes: He means: read the משנה as saying she tears up her כתובה instead of writing a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that receipts are written
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof rests on the word 'receipt,' but the משנה can be read as 'she tears' instead.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה clearly says receipt
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי. The משנה clearly says 'she writes a receipt,' so it cannot just be changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: but the משנה teaches 'she writes a receipt'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's rereading. The actual words of the משנה say receipt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer works only by changing the text. רבא points out that the text plainly says שוברת, so we should explain the משנה as written and not rewrite it.

keyTerms.meaning: She writes a receipt (for her כתובה)
'But it teaches!': pointing to the actual wording

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But it teaches 'she writes a receipt'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's rereading in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's change of the משנה's wording to 'she tears'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה plainly says שוברת. A rereading that goes against the clear text is not acceptable.

steps.title: רבא: a place where no כתובה is written
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the word 'receipt' but still blocks the proof. He says the משנה is talking about a place where people do not write a כתובה, so there is nothing to tear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: we are dealing with a place where they do not write a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer. He keeps the משנה's wording but explains it so that it proves nothing in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a place with no written כתובה, the husband has nothing to tear. A receipt is the only way to show he no longer owes her. So the משנה does not prove that receipts are written in a normal case where a document exists. The proof from step 19 is blocked without changing the משנה's words, and this replaces אביי's rejected reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': replaces the previous answer
'We are dealing with': narrowing the case
In a place where they do not write (a כתובה)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'receipt' is no proof that we always write a שובר. רבא says it is talking about a place with no written כתובה to tear.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
We are dealing with a place where they do not write a Ketubah.
phrases.notes: With no written כתובה, there is nothing to tear, so a receipt is the only option.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's own answer, which avoids his objection to אביי in step 21 and replaces אביי's reading, while still rejecting the proof of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'receipt' shows that receipts are always the way to record payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a place with no written כתובה, so it proves nothing about normal cases.

steps.title: Questioning 'they bring her up' to the Eastern Gates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if she says 'I am pure,' they bring her up to the Eastern Gates. Then it questions the words 'they bring her up.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she says 'I am pure,' they bring her up to the Eastern Gates. They bring her up?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and starts a question about its wording. This sets up a discussion that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprised question 'They bring her up?!' shows that the גמרא finds the phrase 'bring her up' puzzling. The exact difficulty and its answer come next, so for now just notice that the wording is being challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am pure': the סוטה insists she is innocent
They bring her up
The Eastern Gates of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And if she says: 'I am pure,'
they bring her up to the Eastern Gates.
They bring her up?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is surprised by the word 'bring up'. The reason it is puzzling is explained on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'they bring her up'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא finds the wording 'bring her up' hard to understand. The full difficulty is explained in the continuation.
